text:
maria: Heads up — eu-north1 GPU pool didn't scale for ~15m during the provisioning spike. Autoscaler shows low metrics, but Prometheus has no node-exporter data for that window. Anyone see telemetry gaps?

ash: @maria can you paste the prometheus query + rough window? also did we see any pipeline backpressure? :eyes:

maria: querying from 2026-03-17T20:50 -> 2026-03-17T21:05: `rate(node_cpu_seconds_total[5m])` returns flatline. Prometheus scrape logs show 503s to the node-exporter endpoints.

devon: looked at kube logs — fluentd sidecar on the gpu nodes crashed around 21:01 with OOM and then didn't restart fast enough. saw repeated `CrashLoopBackOff`.

maria: partial logs: ```
Mar 17 21:01:12 gpu-node-7 kubelet[1234]: containerd: starting container fluentd:latest
Mar 17 21:01:15 fluentd[1]: ERROR: failed to allocate buffer: NoMemoryError
Mar 17 21:01:16 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4567 (fluentd) score 985 or sacrifice child
Mar 17 21:01:16 kubelet: Back-off restarting failed container
```

ash: that would explain dropped logs and some /metrics pipelines. did node-exporter die too or was it just network egress?

devon: node-exporter was up but Fluentd crash also took down the logging sidecar that forwards driver/kernel logs to our central cluster — so GPU driver errors weren't received by obs. also `curl http://node-exporter:9100/metrics` from a busybox pod returned `Empty reply from server`.

kevin: suggested remediation: restart fluentd DaemonSet and add a short-term Prometheus scrape fallback to pull from `cadvisor` on kubelet if node-exporter response missing. we can patch DS to use `fluentd:stable-20260316` (smaller memory footprint) as a quick rollback. :+1:

ash: executing: ```kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/fluentd && kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=fluentd -o wide```

ash: rollout restart triggered, most pods came back within 40s. observed pod restarts dropping from CrashLoopBackOff -> Running.

infra-bot: Deploy event: rollout/daemonset/fluentd restarted by ash (deploy-id: dpl_7923). autopromote=off.

devon: added a temporary prometheus-relabel job to scrape `kubelet/cadvisor` for node-level metrics while we fix fluentd. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-config/pull/4578 (WIP). this buys us scrapes but not the kernel logs.

maria: kernel/drivers logs are still missing for the outage window. driver errors triggered retries in the provisioning controller; without those logs autoscaler couldn't pick up transient driver failures and kept rescheduling to the same unhealthy nodes. we need a short-term synthetic probe to infer GPU health from device presence + NVML return codes.

devon: created `gpu-health-exporter` prototype that queries NVML and exposes `redwood_gpu_device_status{device="gpu0"}=0/1`. quick patch applied to the gpu node DaemonSet as sidecar. rolling out now.

kevin: good. once gpu-health-exporter is scraped we can use alerting to fail nodes faster, letting autoscaler avoid bad nodes. also need to increase fluentd liveness probe memory headroom and look at Ruby GC config.

ash: opened incident ticket and assigned postmortem: https://boards.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1037 (owner: devon). severity set to P2 because capacity degraded but no customer-facing SLA breach.

devon: merged the small memory-tuning cherry-pick to release branch and backported to `release/2026-03` after smoke tests. PRs: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-config/pull/4578 https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4621

maria: follow-ups: 1) add liveness probe change and RBAC for gpu-health exporter, 2) add synthetic probe to capacity autoscaler to use `redwood_gpu_device_status`, 3) schedule a runbook update for eu-north1 provisioning. I'll create tasks. :memo:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1037 marked resolved by ash — timeline recorded, follow-ups created.

ash: thanks everyone. I'll add a short timeline and link logs to the postmortem. please add any missing notes to the incident board. :white_check_mark:
